resources.string: Pairing lives entirely in the QR you scan — the relay address and token are stored privately in this phone and are never shown or typed.
Streams this phone screen. Android shows a system dialog every time — sharing can never start silently.
Idle — start sharing, then accept the system dialog.
Permission denied — tap Start sharing to retry.
Lets a remote viewer tap, swipe and press Back and Home through the accessibility service.
Remote taps, swipes and system buttons.
Send a test tap to the center of the screen
Control service is off — enable it first.
No focused text field — tap a text field first, or enable control.
Each capability needs your approval. Toggle on — Android opens the system screen where you confirm. Nothing enables silently.
Set a relay URL, enable control, then start sharing.
Screen: off · Control: off · Relay: off
Scan the pairing QR shown on the web viewer (CRM → Mobile → Pair new phone). The relay address and secret token are stored inside this app — nothing to type, nothing on screen.
Web viewer is OPEN — it can see and connect to this phone. (%1$s)
Web viewer is not open. Open the CRM on your computer to connect. (%1$s)
Server not reachable yet — check this phone\'s internet. (%1$s)
Scan the pairing QR from the web viewer first — sharing needs a paired server.
The stored token is removed. You will need to scan a fresh QR to pair again.
Unpaired. Scan the QR on the web viewer to pair again.
Point the camera at the pairing QR on the web viewer page.
That code is not a pairing QR — use the one on the viewer page.
Camera access denied — the scanner needs it to read the pairing QR.
Paired with %1$s — start sharing, then press Connect on the web.
The camera is only used to read the pairing QR from your viewer page. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.
Remote control needs a paired server. Scan the pairing QR shown on the web viewer (CRM → Mobile → Pair new phone) first.
Axie Remote needs two system approvals to inject taps and button presses. Takes about 30 seconds.
Side-loaded apps are blocked until you allow it: App info → menu (top right) → Allow restricted settings. Needed on Android 13 and newer only.
Accessibility settings → Downloaded apps → Axie Control → turn it on.
Still off — finish the steps above, then check again.
Checks the public release feed for a newer signed APK and installs it on this device.
Check failed — retry on a network.
Allow Install unknown apps for Axie Remote, then retry.
Android shows screen sharing through a persistent notification. Without it, sharing still works but you will not see the indicator. You can change this later in App info.
This turns on the Axie Control accessibility service so a remote viewer can tap, swipe and press Back and Home for you. Nothing is enabled until you confirm in system settings.
Lets Axie Remote tap, swipe and press system buttons on your behalf during a remote-control session.
Axie Remote is sharing your screen
